searches.purpose: Locate Japanese primary bibliography, independent socio-history, classical and outpatient method boundaries, century review, controlled evidence, a condition-bounded synthesis, Japanese current institutions and cross-cultural adaptation while distinguishing classical residential Morita therapy from outpatient, dialog-based, UK-adapted, generic acceptance or Constructive Living programmes; no dedicated publicly inspectable profession-specific adverse-event or contraindication guideline met the retrieval threshold

items.title: Work, Self, and Society: A Socio-Historical Study of Morita Therapy
items.rights_note: Open socio-history situates work, self and therapy in 1920s–1930s Japan and complicates timeless Buddhist-only narratives; its work-centered interpretation is not a complete clinical history or outcome assessment.
items.failure_note: The Springer endpoint returned a 3 KB Client Challenge shell; the matching PMC full text was selected without solving the challenge.

items.title: 神経質の本態及び療法
items.rights_note: National Diet Library record identifies Morita's 1928 Japanese foundational work; the record is cached rather than silently substituting the 1960 revised edition or 1998 English translation for the original text.

items.title: Guidelines for Practising Outpatient Morita Therapy: Paired Japanese-English Translation Edition
items.rights_note: Japanese Society consensus guideline and paired translation identify common outpatient components while explicitly allowing modification; outpatient dialogue and diaries must not be represented as the original residential four-stage programme.

items.title: A Century of Morita Therapy: What Has and Has Not Changed
items.rights_note: Open century review distinguishes declining classical inpatient practice, later dialog-based outpatient forms and comparisons with mindfulness and ACT; it is participant historiography and resemblance does not establish equivalence among therapies.

items.title: Morita Therapy for Depression (Morita Trial): A Pilot Randomised Controlled Trial
items.rights_note: Open UK pilot tests feasibility and estimates outcomes for an adapted 8–12-session outpatient protocol in 68 adults with major depression; it was not powered as a definitive efficacy trial and does not test classical residential Morita therapy.

items.title: Morita Therapy for Anxiety Disorders in Adults
items.rights_note: Cochrane review found seven small high-risk-of-bias studies, all conducted in China, and insufficient adverse-effect reporting, so it could not conclude effectiveness; applicability beyond included Chinese settings and combined pharmacotherapy protocols is limited.

items.title: What Is Morita Therapy? The Nature, Origins, and Cross-Cultural Application of a Unique Japanese Psychotherapy
items.rights_note: Open article describes Japanese cultural framing and recommendations from a UK adaptation team; claims of cross-cultural promise remain tied to early feasibility work and must not erase Japanese concepts, setting changes or local therapist training.
items.failure_note: The Springer endpoint returned the same 3 KB Client Challenge shell as another article; the German National Library-hosted open article PDF was selected without solving the challenge.

items.title: 日本森田療法学会
items.rights_note: Official Japanese society site documents current conferences, certification information, institutions and multilingual materials; institutional continuation does not establish efficacy or a single globally regulated credential.
